data.description:
Board request, DM msg 163, 2026-08-30 20:41Z, verbatim: "Also, I'm going to be using this on my phone so let's make it layout mobile friendly". Context: the board member's primary interface with the company is this chat app (CLAUDE.md), and he will use it from a phone — mobile is a first-class surface, not a nice-to-have.

Scope — what 'mobile friendly' means for this app: the web UI at apps/chat/public must be usable on a phone-sized viewport (~375-430px wide). Concretely: (1) responsive layout — the sidebar (channels + DM roster) must not consume the viewport; collapse it behind a toggle/drawer on narrow screens, with the message pane full-width; (2) touch targets and font sizes adequate for touch (no tiny click zones); (3) viewport meta + no horizontal scroll; (4) compose box usable with the on-screen keyboard (doesn't get hidden, input stays visible); (5) the AS-9 URL-state contract keeps working so links shared from phone/desktop open the same view.

Relationship to the other chat UX tasks (all bumped per board msg 160 "let's get going on all the chat UX improvements"): AS-17 (thread scroll position + default identity) is independent. AS-18 (DM pinning/sort) touches the same sidebar this task collapses — coordinate, land AS-18 after or fold its sidebar markup in. AS-19 (threads inline or large modal, retiring the narrow thread sidebar) INTERACTS directly: the thread presentation chosen there determines the mobile thread UX (a modal is naturally full-screen on mobile; inline needs its own narrow-viewport treatment). Sequence AS-19 before this task so the mobile layout is built against the final thread presentation, not the retiring sidebar.

Acceptance: chat is fully usable — read, switch conversations, post, open threads, mark read — in a 390px-wide viewport with no horizontal scroll; desktop layout unchanged.
data.title: Chat UI: mobile-friendly responsive layout

data.body: Filed on behalf of human:forrest from DM msg 163 (2026-08-30). Full decision context and scope in the description. Position 3 in the chat UX queue: AS-17 -> AS-19 -> AS-23 -> AS-18; AS-19's thread-presentation decision is a deliberate prerequisite.

Plan written (agent:cto-owen). Approach: one mobile breakpoint at <=700px — #sidebar becomes an off-canvas drawer (fixed, translateX(-100%), scrim at z 25 / drawer z 26, below the AS-19 backdrop z 30), hamburger in #conv-header, drawer closes on any conversation select (single hook in selectConversation) and never touches the URL (AS-9 projection invariant intact). Touch: (hover:none) unhides .message .actions — hover-gated 'reply in thread' is a functional break on touch, not polish; 40px targets; 16px input font kills iOS focus auto-zoom. Keyboard: 100dvh + a ~12-line visualViewport pin (--app-height) because no CSS unit tracks the iOS keyboard; honestly flagged as device-verifiable only. Global: overflow-x hidden, task-panel width clamped via min(). SCOPE DECISION: Priya's AS-19 backlog item (selection-drag from dialog to backdrop closes the modal) FOLDS IN — same three files, and press-drag selection is the canonical mobile gesture; fix is her sketched pointerdown-target check as a NEW pure predicate (existing thread-modal.js exports and their tests byte-unmodified; test additions only). No separate task filed. Guarded suites: url-state.test.js + scroll.test.js byte-identical to master, thread-modal.test.js additive-only. Acceptance split honestly: A1-A3 container-assertable (served HTML/CSS rules, suites), B1-B8 board phone walk (~2 min, iPhone/Tailscale) — the board IS the mobile QA; checklist written for him verbatim in the plan. Desktop invariance: every new rule inside media/hover guards except three named no-op-at-desktop lines. Sequencing: AS-18 rebases trivially (this touches sidebar positioning, not list contents).

Implementation complete (agent:developer-marcus), 2 commits on feat/AS-23-mobile-layout (2a904f3 selection-drag fix, 31550f2 mobile layout). Suite 136 green in-container (was 132; +3 predicate tests, +1 served-artifact test); also verified via throwaway container on port 8399 (live 8347 untouched). Guards hold: url-state.test.js + scroll.test.js byte-identical to master, thread-modal.test.js purely additive (0 removed lines), existing exports byte-unmodified, STATIC_FILES unchanged. Two boring choices where the plan was ambiguous: (1) drawer close in selectConversation is gated on url==='push' — the 5s poll funnels through selectConversation with url:'none' and an unconditional close would slam a drawer the user is browsing every 5s; 'push' is exactly the set of user picks (sidebar li, roster row, typeahead, new-channel). (2) #conv-header becomes a wrapping flex row at <=700px (toggle+title line one, purpose full-width below) — the plan added the toggle to the header but not its layout; no markup beyond the planned button. Note for QA on A3: two additional top-level rules exist beyond the three named — default display:none for the NEW #sidebar-toggle/#sidebar-scrim elements; they only hide new elements, zero effect on desktop layout. Board-only residual: B1-B8 phone checklist (iOS keyboard behavior is device-only-verifiable; code degrades to 100dvh without visualViewport).
